```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 11,
  fig.height = 7, dpi = 500, fig.retina = 1, crop = FALSE, dev = "png", dev.args = list(type = "cairo"), out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center")
library(GeneTrackR)
library(patchwork)
plain_text <- ggplot2::element_text(family = "Arial", colour = "black", face = "plain")
tutorial_text <- ggplot2::theme(text = plain_text, axis.text = plain_text,
  axis.title = plain_text, plot.title = plain_text, plot.subtitle = plain_text,
  plot.caption = plain_text, legend.text = plain_text, legend.title = plain_text,
  strip.text = plain_text)
classic_style <- ggplot2::theme_classic(base_family = "Arial") + tutorial_text
ggplot2::theme_set(classic_style)
demo_file <- function(name) system.file("extdata", name, package = "GeneTrackR", mustWork = TRUE)
```

# Question and evidence chain

For a candidate region, ask whether genotype-defined groups are associated
with a trait, how local LD relates the sites, and what annotation/signal
context helps prioritize follow-up. This example connects the preceding
workflows without repeating their parameter guides. Package website:
<https://renscq.github.io/GeneTrackR/>.

The inputs are the shared synthetic GeneA system. Signal values, phenotypes
and designed associations are not observations from a real organism. See
[Getting started](getting-started.html) for the comparison with Gviz,
rtracklayer and VariantAnnotation and the data-generation contracts.

# Prepare inputs and check alignment

```{r inputs}
gp <- read_genepred(demo_file("gtr_demo.genePredExt"), format = "genePredExt",
  verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
vcf <- read_vcf(demo_file("gtr_demo_variants.vcf"), mode = "memory",
  keep_genotype = TRUE, verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
pheno <- read_pheno(demo_file("gtr_demo_pheno.tsv"), verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
signal <- read_bwg(demo_file(c("gtr_demo_rnaseq_plus.bedgraph", "gtr_demo_riboseq_plus.bedgraph")),
  sample_names = c("RNA_seq_plus", "Ribo_seq_plus"), strand = c("+", "+"),
  mode = "memory", verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(vcf$meta$sample_names), !anyDuplicated(pheno$sample_id))
shared <- intersect(vcf$meta$sample_names, pheno$sample_id)
data.frame(genotype_n = length(vcf$meta$sample_names), phenotype_n = nrow(pheno),
  shared_n = length(shared), genotype_only = length(setdiff(vcf$meta$sample_names, pheno$sample_id)),
  phenotype_only = length(setdiff(pheno$sample_id, vcf$meta$sample_names)))
stopifnot(length(shared) == 36L)
```

For external data, reconcile genome assembly, chromosome naming, coordinates,
sample identifiers, duplicates and missingness before plotting or testing.
Internal intervals are 1-based closed. Sample joins use IDs rather than row
order. Preserve original inputs and record every exclusion.

# Bring external intervals into the locus

This can be the output of an existing Bioconductor overlap or peak workflow.
The input enters GeneTrackR directly from GRanges.

```{r external-intervals}
external_ranges <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1",
  IRanges::IRanges(c(12339750L, 12342620L), c(12340200L, 12343180L)))
names(external_ranges) <- c("candidate_promoter", "candidate_interval")
external_ranges$score <- c(2.5, 4.5)
features <- as_feature(external_ranges)
returned <- as_granges(features, level = "feature")
stopifnot(length(returned) == 2L, identical(names(returned), names(external_ranges)),
  identical(returned$score, c(2.5, 4.5)))
```

The [range workflow](annotation.html#existing-granges) covers sorting, typed
metadata, names, annotations, sequence information and gene-model limitations.
Those conversion rules also apply to filtered feature objects here.

# Inspect the integrated locus {#integrated-browser}

```{r browser-context}
browser <- plot_tracks(annotation = gp, signal = signal, features = features,
  variants = vcf, chrom = "chr1", start = 12339001L, end = 12374500L,
  samples = c("RNA_seq_plus", "Ribo_seq_plus"), strand = "+", signal_type = "bar",
  signal_colors = c(RNA_seq_plus = "#4477AA", Ribo_seq_plus = "#228833"),
  variant_colors = c(SNP = "#4477AA", INS = "#228833", DEL = "#CC6677"),
  highlight = data.frame(start = 12342620L, end = 12343180L),
  layout = "gene_top", plot_theme = "classic", text_size = 10) & tutorial_text
browser
```

This plot places annotations, signals, external intervals and variants on the
same genomic axis. Signal panels may have different y-axis scales and units;
visual height alone is not a cross-sample normalization or statistical test.
Check strand, transcript structure, track identity and exact variant positions
before selecting follow-up intervals. The [annotation and signal workflow](annotation.html#reading-frame)
executes a transcript-coordinate Ribo-seq reading-frame example.

# Construct groups and compare a trait

```{r genotype-and-trait}
hap <- hap_gene_variant(vcf, annotation = gp, gene_id = "GeneA", genotype_mode = "string")
stopifnot(nrow(hap$variants) == 11L, nrow(hap$haplotypes) == 4L,
  all(hap$haplotypes$sample_n == 9L))
association <- plot_hap_pheno(hap, phenotype = pheno, traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3, test_method = "t.test", p_adjust = "BH",
  p_value_type = "adjusted", text_size = 10)
association$summary
association$pvalue
```

The numeric comparison uses two-sided Welch t-tests and BH-adjusted P values
for the six pairwise comparisons of this trait. The table and group sample
sizes are the evidence; the plot is a display. Interpret effect direction and
units, examine missingness, and assess the assumptions for real samples.

# Add LD and refinement context

```{r ld-and-refinement}
ld <- compute_ld_block(vcf, chrom = "chr1", start = 12342620L, end = 12355500L,
  variant_type = "snp", method = "r2", verbose = FALSE)
stopifnot(nrow(ld$variants) == 12L, nrow(ld$data) == 66L)
head(ld$data)
refined <- refine_haplotype(hap, phenotype = pheno, traits = "protein_content",
  min_hap_samples = 3, effect_threshold = 0.5)
refined$haplotype_map
```

LD identifies correlated genotype patterns, so several associated sites can
carry overlapping evidence. Refinement uses the phenotype already analyzed;
it is exploratory and requires independent validation. Preserve the original
groups and the mapping to refined groups. Detailed methods and result-object
contracts are in [haplotypes/LD](haplotype.html) and
[phenotypes/refinement](phenotype.html).

# Return to Bioconductor and preserve evidence

```{r return-to-bioc}
query <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(12342650L, 12343000L))
hits <- GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(as_granges(features, level = "feature"), query)
as_granges(features, level = "feature")[S4Vectors::queryHits(hits)]
```

The delivered evidence is a coherent set of annotation/variant/signal inputs,
sample-alignment counts, haplotypes, association tables, LD and the original
and refined mappings. These support candidate prioritization, not a causal
claim. Independent populations, functional assays or other appropriate
experiments are still needed for biological confirmation.

Follow [Export and reproducibility](export-results.html) to save standard
tracks, figures, tables, complete objects, parameters and session information.
For very large files, use indexed regional access where supported and inspect
the documented fallback behavior before launching whole-genome analyses.

```{r session-info}
sessionInfo()
```
